This decrease of 27% was driven by lower demand from Africa region, mainly West Africa, and Middle East region. In Africa, this was due to the Coup d’état that occurred in Niger in July 2023 which escalated into a political crisis affecting neighbouring countries in West Africa. Demand from the Middle East weakened as a result of the crisis in the Red Sea region which led to a sharp increase in freight costs affecting shipments to Middle East and East Africa ports. As our primary operations is the export of fast moving consumer goods, the weakened MYR relative to USD throughout FY2024 resulted in favourable average foreign exchange rates to cushion the demand challenges in the financial year under review. The opening of MYR/USD commenced the financial year at MYR 4.60 per 1 USD and peaked at MYR 4.77 in April 2024, ending at MYR 4.71 for June 2024.
